facts.statement: Ornithocheirus is a pterosaur genus named for its 'bird hand' appearance, known from fragmentary fossils found in the UK and possibly Morocco.
facts.quote: Ornithocheirus (from Ancient Greek "ὄρνις", meaning bird, and "χεῖρ", meaning hand) is a pterosaur genus known from fragmentary fossil remains uncovered from sediments in the United Kingdom and possibly Morocco.

facts.statement: Most Ornithocheirus fossils come from the Cambridge Greensand of England, dating to about 110 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossil remains of Ornithocheirus have been recovered mainly from the Cambridge Greensand of England, dating to the beginning of the Albian stage of the early Cretaceous period, about 110 million years ago.

facts.statement: Seeley described 27 species of Ornithocheirus between 1869 and 1870 based on fragmentary material.
facts.quote: Between the years 1869 and 1870, Seeley each gave them a separate species name: O. simus, O. woodwardi, O. oxyrhinus, O. carteri, O. platyrhinus, O. sedgwickii, O. crassidens, O. capito, O. eurygnathus, O. reedi, O. cuvieri, O. scaphorhynchus, O. brachyrhinus, O. colorhinus, O. dentatus, O. denticulatus, O. enchorhynchus, O. xyphorhynchus, O. fittoni, O. nasutus, O. polyodon, O. tenuirostris, O. machaerorhynchus, O. platystomus, O. microdon, O. oweni and O. huxleyi, thus 27 in total.

facts.statement: Sir Richard Owen rejected the name Ornithocheirus in 1870 because he was not an evolutionist and believed the material represented two distinct types based on snout and tooth differences.
facts.quote: When Seeley published his conclusions in his 1870 book The Ornithosauria, this provoked a reaction by the leading British paleontologist of his day, Sir Richard Owen. Owen was not an evolutionist and he therefore considered the name Ornithocheirus to be inappropriate; he also thought it was possible to distinguish two main types within the material, based on differences in snout form and tooth position — the best fossils consisted of jaw fragments.

facts.statement: In 1874, Richard Owen split Ornithocheirus into two new genera, Coloborhynchus ('maimed beak') and Criorhynchus ('ram beak'), based on jaw variations.
facts.quote: In 1874, he created two new genera: Coloborhynchus and Criorhynchus. Coloborhynchus (meaning "maimed beak") which comprised a new type species called Coloborhynchus clavirostris, as well as two other species reassigned from Ornithocheirus: C. sedgwickii and C. cuvieri. Criorhynchus (meaning "ram beak") consisted entirely of former Ornithocheirus species: the type species, Criorhynchus simus, and furthermore such as C. eurygnathus, C. capito, C. platystomus, C. crassidens and C. reedi.

facts.statement: Reginald Walter Hooley in 1914 merged Owen's genera Coloborhynchus and Criorhynchus back into Ornithocheirus.
facts.quote: In 1914 Reginald Walter Hooley made a new attempt to structure the large number of species. Hooley synonymized Owen's Criorhynchus to Ornithocheirus, in which he also sunk Coloborhynchus into that genus, meaning that the only generic name he kept was Ornithocheirus.

facts.statement: The genus Ornithocheirus was established by Harry Seeley in 1870.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Seeley, 1870

facts.statement: The genus Ornithocheirus was originally named by Harry Seeley in 1869.
facts.quote: authority: Seeley, 1869

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Ornithocheirus is O. simus.
facts.quote: type_species: Ornithocheirus simus

facts.statement: Former synonyms of Ornithocheirus include Pterodactylus simus, Criorhynchus simus, and O. platyrhinus.
facts.quote: synonyms: *Pterodactylus simus Owen, 1861 Criorhynchus simus Owen, 1874 Ornithocheirus platyrhinus Seeley, 1870

facts.statement: While some species were once referred to Ornithocheirus from North America, Europe, and South America, O. simus is primarily known from the UK and a possible specimen from Morocco.
facts.quote: Species have been referred to Ornithocheirus from the mid-Cretaceous period of North America, Europe and South America, but O. simus is known mostly from the United Kingdom, though a specimen referred to O. cf. simus is also known from the Late Cretaceous Kem Kem Group of Morocco.

facts.statement: The poor preservation of the original material for O. simus has caused long-standing issues with the classification of the genus Ornithocheirus.
facts.quote: Because O. simus was originally named based on poorly preserved fossil material, the genus Ornithocheirus has suffered enduring problems of zoological nomenclature.

facts.statement: In 2000, David Unwin argued that Criorhynchus was invalid and that O. simus was the correct type species, which allowed the revival of the genus Lonchodectes.
facts.quote: However, in 2000 Unwin stated that Criorhynchus could not be valid. Referring to Seeley's designation of 1881 he considered Ornithocheirus simus, holotype CAMSM B.54428, to be the type species. This also made it possible to revive Lonchodectes, using as type the former O. compressirostris, which then became L. compressirostris.

facts.statement: In 2013, researchers Rodrigues and Kellner determined that Ornithocheirus is monotypic, containing only the species O. simus.
facts.quote: In 2013, Rodrigues and Kellner found Ornithocheirus to be monotypic, containing only O. simus, and placed most other species in other genera, or declared them nomina dubia.

facts.statement: The type species Ornithocheirus simus is known only from fragmentary jaw tips.
facts.quote: The type species, Ornithocheirus simus, is only known from fragmentary jaw tips.

facts.statement: Past estimates suggested Ornithocheirus could have had a wingspan of 40 feet (12.2 meters), though this is now considered exaggerated.
facts.quote: It was believed in the past that Ornithocheirus was one of the largest pterosaurs to have existed, with a wingspan possibly measuring 40 feet (12.2 m) wide.

facts.statement: Modern estimates suggest Ornithocheirus had a wingspan of 15 to 20 feet (4.5 to 6.1 meters), classifying it as a medium-sized pterosaur.
facts.quote: However, this is a highly exaggerated number, as the animal's wingspan likely measured 15 to 20 feet (4.5 to 6.1 m) wide, which would make it a medium-sized pterosaur.

facts.statement: In 2022, Gregory S. Paul estimated Ornithocheirus had a wingspan of 5 meters and a body mass of 20 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2022, Gregory S. Paul estimated that Ornithocheirus had a wingspan of 5 m and a body mass of 20 kg.

facts.statement: In 2019, Pêgas et al. classified Ornithocheirus as a basal member of the clade Ornithocheirae.
facts.quote: In 2019, Pêgas et al. found Ornithocheirus to be in a basal member of the clade Ornithocheirae, reclassifying all other snout-crested pterosaurs in the family Anhangueridae.

facts.statement: A 2025 phylogenetic analysis identified Thapunngaka as the closest relative of Ornithocheirus.
facts.quote: In a 2025 phylogenetic analysis, Thapunngaka was recovered as the closest relative of Ornithocheirus.

facts.statement: Ornithocheirus lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Inferior

facts.statement: Fossils of Ornithocheirus have been recovered mainly from the Cambridge Greensand in England, dating to the early Albian (Early Cretaceous) about 110 million years ago.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles actualmente clasificados como Ornithocheirus han sido recuperados mayormente de Cambridge Greensand en Inglaterra, datando de principios del Albiense en el período Cretácico, hace unos 110 millones de años.

facts.statement: Additional fossils from the Santana Formation in Brazil, dating between 112 and 108 million years ago, have occasionally been classified as Ornithocheirus or placed in other genera like Tropeognathus.
facts.quote: Fósiles adicionales de la formación Santana de Brasil, datando de entre 112 a 108 millones de años, han sido clasificados ocasionalmente como una especie de Ornithocheirus, o ubicados en otros géneros, destacándose Tropeognathus.

facts.statement: The original material of Ornithocheirus simus from England indicates a medium-sized species with a wingspan of 2.5 meters.
facts.quote: El material original de Ornithocheirus simus, recuperado de Inglaterra, indica una especie de tamaño medio con una envergadura de 2.5 metros.

facts.statement: Specimens referred to Ornithocheirus simus (alternatively called Criorhynchus simus) can reach a wingspan of 5 meters.
facts.quote: Especímenes referidos atribuidos a Ornithocheirus simus (alternativamente llamado Criorhynchus simus) pueden alcanzar los 5 metros.

facts.statement: Both O. simus and O. mesembrinus had distinctive convex, keeled crests on their snouts.
facts.quote: Tanto O. simus como O. mesembrinus tenían distintivas crestas convexas en forma de quilla sobre sus hocicos.

facts.statement: Unlike relatives Anhanguera and Coloborhynchus which had tooth rosettes at jaw tips, Ornithocheirus had straight jaws that tapered to a point.
facts.quote: A diferencia de sus parientes Anhanguera y Coloborhynchus, que tenían una roseta de dientes en la punta de sus mandíbulas, Ornithocheirus tenía mandíbulas rectas que se estrechaban hacia la punta.

facts.statement: Unlike other related pterosaurs, the teeth of Ornithocheirus were almost vertical instead of set at an open angle.
facts.quote: A diferencia de otros pterosaurios emparentados, los dientes de Ornithocheirus eran casi verticales, en vez de situarse en un ángulo abierto.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Ornithocheirus simus is represented only by a broken piece of the upper jaw tip.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo de Ornithocheirus simus es representado solo por una pieza rota de la punta de la mandíbula superior.

facts.statement: It is debated whether O. simus and O. mesembrinus are distinct species, as the type specimen of O. simus is nearly identical to comparable bones in O. mesembrinus.
facts.quote: Aunque ésta preserva varios rasgos característicos de Ornithocheirus, es casi idéntica a los huesos comparables en o. mesembrinus, haciendo que una distinción clara entre estas dos especies sea imposible.

facts.statement: Fragmentary pterosaur fossils were found in England within the Cambridge Greensand formation.
facts.quote: Durante el , se hallaron en Inglaterra muchos fósiles fragmentarios de pterosaurios en Cambridge Greensand

facts.statement: The young researcher Harry Govier Seeley was commissioned to organize the pterosaur collection at the Sedgwick Museum in Cambridge.
facts.quote: El joven investigador Harry Govier Seeley fue comisionado para darle orden a la colección de pterosaurios del Museo Sedgwick en Cambridge.

facts.statement: Seeley created the new genus Ornithocheirus, meaning "bird's hand," for the Cambridge Greensand material.
facts.quote: Él pronto concluyó que lo mejor era crear un nuevo género para el material de Cambridge Greensand material al que llamó Ornithocheirus, "mano de ave"

facts.statement: Between 1869 and 1870, Seeley named 28 distinct species within the genus Ornithocheirus.
facts.quote: en 1869 y 1870 le dio a cada una un nombre separado de especie: O. simus, O. woodwardi, O. oxyrhinus, O. carteri, O. platyrhinus, O. sedgwickii, O. crassidens, O. capito, O. eurygnathus, O. reedi, O. cuvieri, O. scaphorhynchus, O. brachyrhinus, O. colorhinus, O. dentatus, O. denticulatus, O. enchorhynchus, O. xyphorhynchus, O. fittoni, O. nasutus, O. polyodon, O. compressirostris, O. tenuirostris, O. machaerorhynchus, O. platystomus, O. microdon, O. oweni y O. huxleyi, hasta 28 en total.

facts.statement: Richard Owen reacted to Seeley's 1870 book The Ornithosauria by disagreeing with the genus name and classification.
facts.quote: Cuando Seeley publicó sus conclusiones en su libro de 1870 The Ornithosauria, provocó la reacción del principal paleontólogo británico de su tiempo, Richard Owen.

facts.statement: In 1874, Richard Owen created two new genera, Coloborhynchus and Criorhynchus, splitting the material previously assigned to Ornithocheirus.
facts.quote: Él en 1874 creó dos nuevos géneros: Coloborhynchus y Criorhynchus.

facts.statement: In 1881, Seeley designated O. simus as the type species of Ornithocheirus and named a new species, O. bunzeli.
facts.quote: En 1881 él designó a O. simus la especie tipo de Ornithocheirus y nombró a una nueva especie, O. bunzeli.

facts.statement: In 1914, Reginald Walter Hooley attempted to reorganize the numerous species of Ornithocheirus.
facts.quote: En 1914 Reginald Walter Hooley hizo un nuevo intento para estructurar el gran número de especies.

facts.statement: In 1978, Peter Wellnhofer designated Ornithocheirus compressirostris as the type species, assuming no type had been previously designated.
facts.quote: En 1978 Peter Wellnhofer, asumiendo que no se había designado una especie tipo, hizo a Ornithocheirus compressirostris el tipo.

facts.statement: Since the 1970s, many new pterosaur fossils have been found in Brazil from formations dating to approximately 110 million years ago.
facts.quote: Desde la década de 1970 en adelante muchos nuevos fósiles de pterosaurios fueron hallados en Brasil, de formaciones que tienen casi la misma edad que Cambridge Greensand, de 110 millones de años de antigüedad.

facts.statement: In 2000, Unwin determined that the genus Criorhynchus was invalid.
facts.quote: En 2000 Unwin estableció que Criorhynchus no podía ser válido.

facts.statement: David Unwin considered Tropeognathus mesembrinus to be Ornithocheirus mesembrinus in 2003.
facts.quote: Tropeognathus mesembrinus nombrado por Peter Wellnhofer en 1987 ha sido posteriormente considerado como Ornithocheirus mesembrinus por David Unwin en 2003

facts.statement: Species originally classified as birds, including Cimoliornis diomedeus, Cretornis hlavatschi, and Palaeornis clifti, were once referred to Ornithocheirus but are now recognized as distinct.
facts.quote: Cimoliornis diomedeus, Cretornis hlavatschi y Palaeornis clifti, originalmente clasificados como aves, fueron referidos anteriormente a Ornithocheirus en el pasado, pero recientemente se los ha reconocido como distintos de Ornithocheirus.

facts.statement: An enormous pterosaur identified as Ornithocheirus was featured in an episode of the BBC series Walking with Dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Un pterosaurio enorme identificado como Ornithocheirus fue representado en un episodio de la premiada serie de televisión de la BBC Walking with Dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Ornithocheirus belongs to the parent group Ornithocheiroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ornithocheiroidea

facts.statement: Ornithocheirus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Ornithocheirus lived from the Hauterivian to the Turonian stages, between 132.6 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Turonian (132.6 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Decomposing pterosaur carcasses floated on the sea surface, losing bones that sank to the ocean floor where they were eventually fossilized.
facts.quote: Los cadáveres descompuestos de pterosaurios, flotando sobre la superficie del mar, fueron gradualmente perdiendo huesos individuales que se hundieron en el fondo del mar.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the genus Criorhynchus is valid, with Unwin rejecting its validity in 2000 despite earlier revivals by other researchers.
facts.quote: Unwin revivió a Coloborhynchus y Michael Fastnacht a Criorhynchus, y ambos autores adscribieron especies brasileñas a estos géneros. Sin embargo, en 2000 Unwin estableció que Criorhynchus no podía ser válido.

facts.statement: Even the largest remains of Ornithocheirus are damaged and difficult to interpret due to the fossilization process involving erosion and burial in sand.
facts.quote: Incluso los mayores de estos restos están dañados y son difíciles de interpretar.
